newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI BOURSE SAYS DISTRIBUTION MUST BE CHECKED.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI BOURSE SAYS DISTRIBUTION MUST BE CHECKED.

text.p: The Helsinki Stock Exchange will advise listed companies to check at once their distribution channels of price-sensitive information, the bourse's managing director Juhani Erma said on Tuesday.
"Whatever the distribution channel, it must not be such that the information can become available at different times," Erma told Reuters by telephone.
"Information must be distributed simultaneously to the bourse and to the media," he said, referring to official stock exchange guidelines.
"We will draw companies' attention to this ... that they must not use such (distribution) tools that the information can be released too early," Erma said.
The bourse would investigate in detail the two recent cases where interim reports had been published by the media before being sent to the stock exchange, he said.

Last week, UPM-Kymmene's H1 results were published by daily Helsingin Sanomat the same day they were due for publication. On Tuesday, Stockmann's H1 results were published by the Finnish news agency a few hours ahead of the announced release time.
Erma said it was too early to say what kind of disciplinary action, if any, the bourse would take regarding these specific incidents. Cases like these have been rare, he added.
Both companies said some copies of their interim reports sent in advance to the post for delivery by mail had been distributed too early by accident.
